C-VV-REBIND-TUI-COMMAND.Summary: Add a /vv-rebind native TUI slash command that re-resolves the effective vvoc configuration for the current session's family by writing the existing project-scoped rebind request marker with the active session id, so the family rebinds to the current configuration on its next workload without leaving the session, opening a terminal, or knowing session ids; no new server-side rebind logic, no diff output, no argument surface.
C-VV-REBIND-TUI-COMMAND.Problem: The only way to move a bound family to the current configuration today is a CLI force flag (vvoc preset apply, plugin enable or disable, role set or unset with --force), which requires leaving the session, running a terminal command in the right project directory, and passing --session to narrow the rebind to one family. A user who discovers mid-session that the family was bound under a wrong configuration, for example a stale project .vvoc/vvoc.json that shadowed the global web key or disabled a plugin, has no in-session way to recompute the policy: the family stays frozen until a CLI force or a server restart, and symptoms like a non-working web search surface far from their cause. The rebind mechanism itself already exists as a project-scoped marker consumed lazily on the family's next workload; only the TUI entry point is missing.

Goals.Goal: Register a /vv-rebind slash command in the native OpenCode TUI beside /context, enabled exactly while a session is open.
On run, write exactly one rebind request marker through the existing src/lib/rebind-request.ts writer, scoped to the TUI working directory, carrying the active session id as the family selector.

Apply the rebind through the existing lazy consumer on the family's next workload, so the very next message already runs under the re-resolved configuration, family-wide (root plus forks and subagents).

Keep inherited semantics unchanged: models switch only when the resolved selection actually changed, and a byte-identical re-resolved policy reuses the same content-addressed snapshot as an observable no-op.
Give the user one bounded feedback line (toast) on run and a bounded hint when no session is open; never include configuration content or credential values in output.

Document /vv-rebind in README beside the --force flags, including the relationship to the native host /reload and the note that credential fields are already re-attached from the live configuration on every request.

Constraints.Constraint: No new server-side rebind logic, no marker format change, and no new CLI command; the TUI command is a third facade over the same marker mechanism as the CLI force flags.
No diff or preview output and no arguments or flags on the command.
The command follows the existing default TUI module enablement (the context toggle gates the whole TUI module) and gets no separate plugin toggle.
Feedback is a single bounded toast; error paths reuse bounded error rendering; no credential value and no configuration content is ever displayed.
The marker write stays atomic and credential-free through the existing writer; the command performs no other filesystem access and no configuration parsing.
No change to the lazy consumer, the marker TTL, family semantics, or fail-soft behavior: an invalid effective configuration still keeps the current family binding.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No eager or immediate rebind; application stays lazy on the family's next workload by design.
No per-field granularity (models versus policy versus orchestration); a rebind changes only what actually changed in the re-resolved configuration.
No drift indicator, diff view, or status output beyond the single feedback line.
No reload of native host configuration; the host /reload remains a separate mechanism.
No caching or IO optimization work around live configuration reads.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: AC-01: With the default TUI module enabled, /vv-rebind appears in the slash palette and is enabled exactly while a session is open; running it with no open session shows a bounded hint and writes no marker.
AC-02: With an open session, one run writes exactly one rebind request marker whose directory resolves to the TUI working directory and whose sessionId equals the active session id.

AC-03: The existing lazy consumer applies the marker on the family's next workload and moves the family pointer to the current revision; when the re-resolved policy projection is identical the snapshot hash is unchanged.

AC-04: Model switching, worker versus root behavior, explicit-selection handling, and fail-soft on an invalid configuration are unchanged from the implemented rebind semantics; the command adds no switching of its own.
AC-05: The command emits one bounded success line naming the next-message application and never displays configuration content, paths beyond the working directory, or credential values.

AC-06: README documents /vv-rebind with the --force flags, the family-wide scope, the next-message timing, and the native /reload distinction; targeted TUI tests, bun run check, and grace lint pass with fresh output.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Fresh tests proving the command registration and enablement, the exact marker written for the active session (directory and sessionId), the no-session hint path with no marker, bounded single-line output without configuration content, plus a passing bun run check, bun run build, and grace lint; README updated beside the force flags.

Assumptions.Assumption: The native TUI command context exposes the active session id the same way /context resolves it, and a keymap-registered command can be added beside the existing context command in the default TUI module.

The TUI process working directory equals the session family's location directory used for marker matching; a session running in another worktree requires running the command from that project, documented in README.
An unconsumed marker is pruned by the existing TTL, so a command run on a session that never works again leaves no permanent state.
